jobs.title: Senior Manager, Development Test Operations Program Management
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.

The Aurora Driver will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.

At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn.

 

What we are looking for

We’re searching for a Senior Manager of Program Management for our Development Test Operations. This manager will manage a team of Program Managers, each embedded as the single point of contact with an engineering group. This role is accountable for setting a program vision, coordinating the portfolio, and setting strong governance and standards for the PM team - turning a group of individually strong PMs into a standardized, predictable program management organization. The Senior Manager must be fluent enough in engineering/development workflows to pressure-test PM decisions, unblock technical escalations, and represent the team credibly with Engineering leadership.

In this role you will

  • Own strategic planning and alignment for the team, including setting the vision for program management, coordinating test programs/portfolio and resourcing, and setting governance and standards

  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of Program Managers, establishing consistent operating norms to increase program quality.

  • Own program-level planning and quality across all engineering areas the team supports (lane and network expansion, track testing, road testing, and other development test workstreams), ensuring every initiative has clear scope, description, and need-by dates, every ticket has a clear, executable test procedure, and operations is receiving high-quality testing requests.

  • Ensure every PM operates as the single point of contact with their engineering area, with clear communication on timelines and needs to/from Engineering and Planning; own the defined escalation path for conflicts and ensure PMs know when to use it.

  • Manage resources, budget, and track dependencies

  • Share test program risks and mitigations with relevant stakeholders

  • Review test execution and QA quality trends across the team, especially on blocked tickets, and drive root-cause process fixes rather than one-off firefighting, closing the feedback loop with both Engineering and Operations.

  • Drive process improvement by moving the team onto standardized workflows, supporting metrics development, and establishing a weekly reporting cadence

Required qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in Program Management, Project Management, or Technical Operations, including 5+ years directly managing a team of Program/Project Managers.

  • Demonstrated experience building or standardizing a reporting and operating cadence across a distributed team, replacing informal coordination with repeatable process.

  • Strong technical fluency across software and hardware development workflows, with the ability to translate engineering plans and progress into concrete, executable field test programs.

  • Proven experience managing relationships and expectations with both Engineering leadership and Planning/Portfolio stakeholders simultaneously.

  • Experience supporting technical or development programs in a cross-functional, fast-paced environment with shifting priorities.

  • Track record of driving change management and process improvement across a team, not just an individual workstream.

Desirable qualifications

  • Experience in autonomous vehicle, automotive, robotics, logistics, or similarly complex operational environments.

  • Exposure to a broad range of test types - field/operational testing, software/feature validation, and platform bring-up or hardware readiness - and comfort moving between them.

  • Familiarity with the software development lifecycle and how development milestones (builds, releases, feature rollouts) map to test scheduling and readiness across varied test types.

  • Experience building or owning dashboards/reporting tools that aggregate program status across multiple sub-teams.

The base salary range for this position is $176,000 - $213,000 per year. Aurora’s pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, the successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on factors including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, relevant education or training, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future. The successful candidate will also be eligible for an annual bonus, equity compensation, and benefits.

Working at Aurora

At Aurora, we bring together extraordinarily talented and experienced people united by the strength of our values. We operate with integrity, set outrageous goals, and build a culture where we win together — all without any jerks.

We believe in-person work increases collaboration, empathy, and our ability to lead effectively. As a result, Aurorans are expected to work from the office at least 3 days per week, with some roles requiring more frequent in-office presence, up to 5 days per week, based on operational needs.

Our Careers page provides insight into what it is like to work at Aurora, and you can find all the latest updates in our Newsroom.

Our commitment to safety

At the core of everything we do is our commitment to safety. Building best-in-class self-driving technology will take time, and we believe that each employee at Aurora has a role in contributing to safety, every step of the way. Aurora expects commitment to our safety policies from every employee, and seeks candidates who take an active responsibility, can contribute to building an atmosphere of trust, and invest in the organization’s long-term success by prioritizing working safely, no matter what.

Our commitment to inclusion

Aurora considers candidates without regard to their race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy status, parent or caregiver status, ancestry, political affiliation, veteran and/or military status, physical or mental disability, or any other status protected by federal or state law. Aurora considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at careersiteaccommodations@aurora.tech.

For California applicants, information collected and processed as part of your application and any job applications you choose to submit is subject to Aurora’s California Employment Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Test Execution (Weekends)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.

The Aurora Driver will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.

At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn.

 

What we are looking for

Aurora hires talented people with diverse backgrounds who are ready to help build a transportation ecosystem that will make our roads safer, get crucial goods where they need to go, and make mobility more efficient and accessible for all.

We’re searching for a Senior Program Manager, Test Execution (Weekend). Aurora's Product Operations team plays a critical role in turning development priorities into safe, executable testing outcomes. This role provides dedicated weekend and adjacent-day (Thursday - Monday) on-site coverage across all Development Testing Operations work-streams, ensuring engineering teams have consistent program management support.

This Program Manager acts as the single point of contact for all assigned engineering areas during the weekend window, standing in for the full team of workstream PMs. You are the first line of defense for test execution questions and escalations, the direct escalation point for on-site issues, and the bridge to leadership when problems can't be resolved.

This is functionally an irregular-operations (IROPs) role: the weekday team builds the plan, and you deliver it. The job isn't to wait for direction; it's to develop and work a known set of playbooks, make the call within defined limits, and know exactly when to pick up the phone to escalate.

This role requires breadth over depth: rather than owning a single engineering relationship, you need working fluency across all the workstreams the team supports so you can triage confidently on your own during the window when the rest of the team is offline.

In This Role, You Will

  • Serve as the direct escalation point for all Program Managers' workstreams during the Saturday-Sunday coverage window, resolving first-tier test execution questions and issues and looping in the right people (Engineering, Safety, Operations, leadership) when they exceed first-tier scope.

  • Own and execute pre-built response playbooks and flag gaps in those playbooks back to the weekday teams

  • Define and work within a decision-authority matrix: know without checking which calls you're empowered to make solo, which need a same-day heads-up to leadership, and which require an immediate escalation before proceeding.

  • Make real-time, hands-on calls on resource substitution — reassigning available assets, adjusting test sequencing, or re-routing around a blocked track/route — to keep the weekend plan moving without waiting for Monday.

  • Support test execution questions and escalations across the full breadth of engineering areas the team covers, not just a single workstream.

  • Review the previous week's plan against actual execution and author the weekly status/summary report on how the week went

  • Recommend and make pivots to the upcoming week's plan based on weekend execution results, blockers, and on-the-ground changes (weather, asset downtime, route/track issues).

  • Track and communicate blockers, delays, and anomalies to stakeholders in a timely manner, using judgment on when an issue needs to go straight to leadership versus being resolved at the PM level.

  • Maintain clear documentation of weekend decisions, pivots, and escalations so the Monday–Friday team has full continuity into the new week.

  • Contribute to a living contingency playbook: after each weekend, document any novel failure mode encountered and the resolution

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in Program Management, Project Management, Product Operations, Technical Operations, or a related role.

  • Demonstrated ability to operate independently and make sound first-tier decisions without real-time access to the full weekday team or leadership.

  • Working knowledge across multiple engineering/test workstreams, with the ability to quickly get oriented on unfamiliar issues.

  • Ability to develop a functional understanding of hardware/software stacks, including how sensors, calibration, and software versions interact to impact vehicle behavior.

  • Strong organizational and written/verbal communication skills, with comfort producing clear status reports and escalating to leadership when needed.

  • Safety focused, with the ability to operate effectively in environments where safety is a core requirement.

  • Required to work a Thursday–Monday schedule, including weekend on-site presence.

  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment with shifting priorities and incomplete information.

  • Comfortable making resourceful, hands-on calls under incomplete information — improvising a workaround, reallocating an available asset, or adjusting a test sequence in the moment rather than escalating by default.

Desirable Qualifications

  • Experience covering or backstopping multiple PM workstreams simultaneously, or prior experience in a "floating" or on-call operational role.

  • Proven experience managing relationships and expectations with senior leadership, escalating appropriately without over- or under-escalating.

  • Comfort using basic data, dashboards, or reporting to support prioritization and execution decisions.

  • Experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive, robotics, logistics, or similarly complex operational environments.

The base salary range for this position is $100,000 - $145,000 per year. Aurora’s pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, the successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on factors including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, relevant education or training, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future. The successful candidate will also be eligible for an annual bonus, equity compensation, and benefits.

Working at Aurora

At Aurora, we bring together extraordinarily talented and experienced people united by the strength of our values. We operate with integrity, set outrageous goals, and build a culture where we win together — all without any jerks.

We believe in-person work increases collaboration, empathy, and our ability to lead effectively. As a result, Aurorans are expected to work from the office at least 3 days per week, with some roles requiring more frequent in-office presence, up to 5 days per week, based on operational needs.

Our Careers page provides insight into what it is like to work at Aurora, and you can find all the latest updates in our Newsroom.

Our commitment to safety

At the core of everything we do is our commitment to safety. Building best-in-class self-driving technology will take time, and we believe that each employee at Aurora has a role in contributing to safety, every step of the way. Aurora expects commitment to our safety policies from every employee, and seeks candidates who take an active responsibility, can contribute to building an atmosphere of trust, and invest in the organization’s long-term success by prioritizing working safely, no matter what.

Our commitment to inclusion

Aurora considers candidates without regard to their race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy status, parent or caregiver status, ancestry, political affiliation, veteran and/or military status, physical or mental disability, or any other status protected by federal or state law. Aurora considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at careersiteaccommodations@aurora.tech.

For California applicants, information collected and processed as part of your application and any job applications you choose to submit is subject to Aurora’s California Employment Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Development Testing Operations (Release Testing)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.

The Aurora Driver will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.

At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn.

 

What we are looking for

Aurora's Product Operations team plays a critical role in ensuring new software releases are validated with rigor and speed before they reach our commercial fleet. We partner closely with Engineering, Safety, and Release Management to make sure every release - onboard and offboard - passes through well-defined, consistently executed test gates.

We’re searching for a Senior Program Manager, Development Testing Operations (Release Testing) to own the test procedures that gate software releases, drive operational excellence in how those tests are executed, and close the feedback loop between test results and engineering. This is a hands-on role for someone who thinks in terms of process rigor, repeatability, and continuous improvement - not just getting a release out the door, but making sure it's actually ready. You are the owner of "did we test this the right way, and did we act on what we learned."

In This Role, You Will

  • Own release test procedures - maintain, version, and continuously improve the test plans, checklists, and standard operating procedures used to gate software releases, ensuring they stay current with engineering requirements and release cadence.

  • Communicate with stakeholders - Work with stakeholders to clearly communicate release timelines across engineering and operations

  • Ensure operational excellence in test execution - define clear pass/fail and escalation criteria, audit test runs for procedural adherence, and drive consistency so releases are tested the same rigorous way every time, minimizing re-work and re-testing.

  • Close the feedback loop - triage test failures and coverage gaps into actionable engineering tickets, track them to resolution, and ensure lessons learned from each release cycle are incorporated back into test procedures rather than lost.

  • Serve as a key input to release gating decisions - partner with Release Management and Engineering to confirm test evidence is complete and current ahead of go/no-go decisions.

  • Identify and reconcile gaps across test types - compare coverage across different stages of the release testing pipeline (e.g., component-level checks vs. full-release regression) to catch blind spots before they become production issues.

  • Drive continuous improvement of the testing program - lead initiatives to streamline test scope, reduce cycle time, and improve signal quality, balancing coverage against speed and cost.

  • Report status and risk - provide regular, clear updates to Engineering, Release Management, and Ops leadership on testing progress, blockers, and release readiness.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in Program Management, Project Management, Quality Assurance, Release Engineering, or a related role

  • Demonstrated experience owning or improving test procedures, QA processes, or release/quality gates in a technical environment

  • Ability to develop a functional understanding of how software releases move through a testing pipeline, including regression testing and staged rollout concepts

  • Experience driving process improvement and change management within a cross-functional organization

  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple test cycles and competing priorities

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with comfort translating technical test results into risk and status reporting for stakeholders at multiple levels

  • Comfort operating in environments where safety and quality are core requirements

  • Ability to support being part of an on-call rotation

  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment with shifting release schedules

Desirable Qualifications

  • Experience with release management, CI/CD pipelines, or regression testing frameworks in a technology or engineering-driven organization

  • Familiarity with defect/issue tracking and test management tooling (e.g., Jira, TestRail, or equivalent)

  • Proven experience managing relationships and expectations with senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders

  • Comfort using dashboards or reporting tools to track test coverage, defect trends, and release readiness

  • Experience in autonomous vehicle, automotive, robotics, or similarly safety-critical operational environments

  • Passion for shipping reliable, high-quality releases and adapting to new responsibilities as the testing program scales

Within the range, the successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on factors including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, relevant education or training, and market conditions. We partner closely with Engineering, Safety, and Release Management to make sure every release - onboard and offboard - passes through well-defined, consistently executed test gates.

We’re searching for a Senior Program Manager, Development Testing Operations (Release Testing) to own the test procedures that gate software releases, drive operational excellence in how those tests are executed, and close the feedback loop between test results and engineering. This is a hands-on role for someone who thinks in terms of process rigor, repeatability, and continuous improvement - not just getting a release out the door, but making sure it's actually ready. You are the owner of "did we test this the right way, and did we act on what we learned."

In This Role, You Will

 - Own release test procedures - maintain, version, and continuously improve the test plans, checklists, and standard operating procedures used to gate software releases, ensuring they stay current with engineering requirements and release cadence.

 - Communicate with stakeholders - Work with stakeholders to clearly communicate release timelines across engineering and operations

 - Ensure operational excellence in test execution - define clear pass/fail and escalation criteria, audit test runs for procedural adherence, and drive consistency so releases are tested the same rigorous way every time, minimizing re-work and re-testing.

 - Close the feedback loop - triage test failures and coverage gaps into actionable engineering tickets, track them to resolution, and ensure lessons learned from each release cycle are incorporated back into test procedures rather than lost.

 - Serve as a key input to release gating decisions - partner with Release Management and Engineering to confirm test evidence is complete and current ahead of go/no-go decisions.

 - Identify and reconcile gaps across test types - compare coverage across different stages of the release testing pipeline (e.g., component-level checks vs. full-release regression) to catch blind spots before they become production issues.

 - Drive continuous improvement of the testing program - lead initiatives to streamline test scope, reduce cycle time, and improve signal quality, balancing coverage against speed and cost.

 - Report status and risk - provide regular, clear updates to Engineering, Release Management, and Ops leadership on testing progress, blockers, and release readiness.

Required Qualifications

 - 5+ years of experience in Program Management, Project Management, Quality Assurance, Release Engineering, or a related role

 - Demonstrated experience owning or improving test procedures, QA processes, or release/quality gates in a technical environment

 - Ability to develop a functional understanding of how software releases move through a testing pipeline, including regression testing and staged rollout concepts

 - Experience driving process improvement and change management within a cross-functional organization

 - Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple test cycles and competing priorities

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills, with comfort translating technical test results into risk and status reporting for stakeholders at multiple levels

 - Comfort operating in environments where safety and quality are core requirements

 - Ability to support being part of an on-call rotation

 - Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment with shifting release schedules

Desirable Qualifications

 - Experience with release management, CI/CD pipelines, or regression testing frameworks in a technology or engineering-driven organization

 - Familiarity with defect/issue tracking and test management tooling (e.g., Jira, TestRail, or equivalent)

 - Proven experience managing relationships and expectations with senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders

 - Comfort using dashboards or reporting tools to track test coverage, defect trends, and release readiness

 - Experience in autonomous vehicle, automotive, robotics, or similarly safety-critical operational environments

 - Passion for shipping reliable, high-quality releases and adapting to new responsibilities as the testing program scales
